objective: Build a versioned JSON REST API (/api/v1) covering every admin and end-user control-plane capability, then reduce the server-rendered panel and admin pages to thin static clients that talk only to that API. Governs and supersedes the admin/panel work in the Steps 5-8 hardening.
tech_stack: Go 1.27, CGO_ENABLED=0, modernc.org/sqlite, net/http ServeMux (Go 1.22+ patterns), no router dep, no JS build toolchain, go:embed assets.
goals: One authoritative HTTP surface (/api/v1) for every control-plane operation available to end users and admins.

Zero business logic in HTTP handlers — thin handlers call store directly (no internal/core layer); thin orchestration ONLY where cross-store (backup config -> scheduler, proofs verify wiring, capabilities derivation).
Machine-checkable contract: hand-written OpenAPI 3.1 spec + bidirectional CI drift test (kin-openapi, test-only dep).
Thin clients: embedded static HTML/CSS/ES-module bundles, no framework, no CDN.
Typed DTOs throughout — no map[string]any in any response.
non_goals: Changing data-plane protocol surfaces (/rs/, /solid/, /xrpc/, /.well-known/*, /profile/) — spec-defined, stay as-is.
Replacing OIDC provider routes (zitadel/oidc at / on identity host).
A JS build toolchain (no bundler, no npm in default task chain).

architectural_decisions.D-1: Control plane lives ONLY on the identity host (id.<domain>/api/v1). Tenant derived from authenticated principal, never Host or body field. [USER-APPROVED]
architectural_decisions.D-2: Routing via stdlib net/http.ServeMux Go 1.22+ patterns. No router dependency.
architectural_decisions.D-4: REVISED: handlers call store directly; no internal/core/* layer. Thin orchestration layer ONLY where cross-store orchestration exists (backup config -> scheduler, proofs verify wiring, capabilities derivation). Store is net/http-free.
architectural_decisions.D-5: Hand-written OpenAPI spec is source of truth; test asserts route-set <-> spec parity both directions. [USER-APPROVED]
architectural_decisions.D-6: Browser auth = HttpOnly session cookie + double-submit CSRF token + Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site. Programmatic auth = Authorization: Bearer only. Mutually exclusive per request.
architectural_decisions.D-7: Keep no-JS fallback for ToS accept and profile edit via form-POST adapters (303-redirect). WebAuthn stays JS-only. [USER-APPROVED]
architectural_decisions.D-8: Each data plane gets its own audience: sovereign-api, sovereign-rs, sovereign-solid, sovereign-atproto.
architectural_decisions.D-9: Self-host simple.css via go:embed; strict CSP with no external origins.

constraints: All gates pass before commit: task lint, test -race, vet, vulncheck, coverage >=80% total AND per-package.
Tenant-scoping: never trust client-supplied tenant/account ID without checking authenticated principal.
No new runtime deps except test-only kin-openapi; justify any addition (GPL-compat, CGO-free).
PII redaction: never log key material, tokens, full proof payloads at info level. GET /invite/{token} token-in-URL leaks via Referer/access logs are acknowledged under this discipline.
No html/template outside web/ and internal/protocols/hyperlink at end of Phase 7.
Handlers stay thin (parse -> call store -> encode); coverage concentrates in store/.
No map[string]any in any response (Step 8 typing).

prerequisites.P-1: Fix scope matching: wiring.go ScopesContains uses strings.HasPrefix(granted, want) — unsound (profile:read-only satisfies profile:read). Replace with exact match + explicit scopeImplies implication table. Land ALONE with regression test per existing call site.
prerequisites.P-2: Real session model: add sessions table (id, user_id, token_hash, created_at, last_seen_at, expires_at, revoked_at, user_agent_hash, ip_hash) with sliding renewal, server-side revocation, absolute cap. Ship with dual-read (accept old JWT cookies AND new session rows) for one release then drop, gated by auth.session.dual_read (default TRUE). SAME cookie name; format-sniffed (JWT parse vs session-token lookup); both formats present -> 400.
prerequisites.P-3: CSRF infrastructure: no CSRF code exists. Double-submit token (__Host-csrf cookie + X-CSRF-Token header) + Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site enforcement for cookie principals on unsafe methods. ALSO accept token from hidden form field (csrf_token) for application/x-www-form-urlencoded POSTs (synchronizer-token, rendered server-side) so no-JS forms work.
prerequisites.P-4: Migrations: sessions, idempotency_keys, backup_config, backup_runs, backup_restores, takedowns, tos_documents, pending_deletions (id, user_id, requested_at, status, approved_by, approved_at), + updated_at/version on users/public_keys/proof_claims/profile_links (ETag on GET).
prerequisites.P-5: Store methods: SetUserDisplayName, UpdateProfileLink, DeleteWebAuthnCredential (refuse last), GetTenantByID, GetTenantByDID, ListUsersPage, ListAuditPage, ListClientsPage, ListTenantsPage, CountUsers, DeleteUser.

api_conventions.versioning: URL path major version; additive within v1; breaking => v2 alongside.
api_conventions.media_types: application/json; charset=utf-8 requests/responses; application/problem+json errors; multipart/form-data for avatar only; application/x-www-form-urlencoded for no-JS form POSTs (with hidden csrf_token field).
api_conventions.collections: Admin lists: {"data":[...],"offset":N,"limit":N,"total":N}. Audit log (genuinely unbounded): {"data":[...],"next_cursor":"..."|null}. Never a bare array.
api_conventions.pagination: Admin lists: offset/limit (?limit=1..200&offset=). Audit log: opaque cursor ?limit=1..200&cursor=. Cursor = base64(sort_key,id).
api_conventions.sorting: Fixed per collection, documented. No arbitrary ?sort=.
api_conventions.concurrency: ETag on single-resource GET (cheap, useful for caching). NO mandatory If-Match on PUT/PATCH/DELETE (single-user server, no concurrent-writer contention).
api_conventions.idempotency: Idempotency-Key header required on POSTs with genuine external side effects (invite send, backup run, backup restore); 24h retention; replay returns original response; email sent only on first execution inside the idempotent handler. IPFS pin is a natural no-op (no Idempotency-Key).
api_conventions.body_limits: MaxBytesReader per route (64 KiB JSON default, 2 MiB avatar) -> 413.
api_conventions.caching: Authenticated: no-store. Public reads: public, max-age=60. All: X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, Vary: Origin, Authorization, Cookie.
api_conventions.cors: Deny by default; allowlist only via api.cors_origins config; never * alongside credentials.
api_conventions.request_id: X-Request-Id echoed/generated; included in every problem response as instance and every log line.
api_conventions.rate_limits: Per-IP token bucket only (no per-principal buckets); 429 with Retry-After + RateLimit-* headers.
api_conventions.method_semantics: PUT full replace, PATCH RFC 7396 merge-patch, POST /collection create, POST /resource:action for non-CRUD verbs (colon suffix).
api_conventions.problem_types: Stable URIs under https://<domain>/problems/: invalid-request, validation-failed (with errors[] of {field, code, detail}), unauthenticated, insufficient-scope, forbidden, not-found, conflict, precondition-required, precondition-failed, payload-too-large, rate-limited, not-implemented, internal.
api_conventions.status_discipline: Never 500 for client error. 403 for scope/role failure. 404 (not 403) for cross-tenant resources (no tenant-enumeration oracle).

principals.end_user_browser: session cookie + CSRF token; scopes derived from user record: self:*, profile:*, keys:*, proofs:*, sessions:*, tokens:*, export:*, account:delete.
principals.end_user_programmatic: bearer, audience sovereign-api; granted subset requested at issue (self-issued via POST /me/tokens, show-once).
principals.admin: as above + IsAdmin on user record; admin:* scopes require BOTH scope AND user.IsAdmin.
principals.invite_bearer: one-time invite token; exchange-only for programmatic: may call POST /auth/invite/redeem and nothing else. Browser GET /invite/{token} is ANONYMOUS (exempt from authn middleware), redeems token, mints SESSION cookie, 303s to /panel.

scope_taxonomy: self profile keys proofs sessions tokens export account
admin:tenants admin:users admin:clients admin:backup admin:moderation admin:audit admin:ipfs admin:system
authn_authz_model.scope_granularity: Coarse scopes (C2): self, profile, keys, proofs, sessions, tokens, export, account, admin:* (with admin:tenants/users/clients/backup/moderation/audit/ipfs/system as the coarse granularity). Read/write implied by scope; scopeImplies table is small and explicit (e.g. profile:write implies profile:read).
middleware_chain: request-id -> panic-recover -> body-limit -> per-route timeout (route-table column; backup run/restore long-running) -> CORS (api.cors_origins) -> rate-limit (per-IP) -> authn (bearer XOR cookie; audience-checked; dual-read format-sniffed, both formats -> 400) -> CSRF (cookie principals, unsafe methods; hidden csrf_token field for form-encoded no-JS POSTs) -> scope authz (declared per route, table-driven, coarse scopes) -> conditional-request (ETag on GET only) -> idempotency (invite + backup run/restore) -> handler -> problem+json mapper -> access log
authn_authz_model.rule: Every route declares its required scope AND its per-route timeout in the route table, so a single test can assert no route has an empty scope requirement.

package_layout.internal/api: router.go (route table: scope + timeout per route), problem/, dto/, middleware/, v1/ (auth, me, profile, keys, proofs, credentials, sessions, admin_*, meta, public).
package_layout.internal/store: net/http-free persistence + business logic; handlers call store directly (C1).
package_layout.internal/web: embed.go (go:embed dist), shared/api.js, shared/simple.css (vendored D-9), panel/ (index.html, panel.js), admin/ (index.html, admin.js).
package_layout.internal/legacyforms: no-JS form adapters over store (D-7), rendering hidden csrf_token field (B1).

auth_session: GET /auth/session (current principal, tenant, scopes, onboarding state)
POST /auth/webauthn/login/begin|finish (anon, uniform response for unknown handles)
GET /invite/{token} ANONYMOUS browser entry point: redeems token, mints SESSION cookie, 303 /panel (not exchange-only; token-in-URL leak acknowledged)
self: DELETE /me (account:delete) -> REQUEST + admin approval via pending_deletions [USER-APPROVED decision 4]
GET/POST /me/tokens (POST creates programmatic token, show-once, scope-subset selection), DELETE /me/tokens/{family_id}
admin: POST /admin/users/{id}/invites (Idempotency-Key required; email sent inside idempotent handler)
GET/POST /admin/ipfs/pins, GET /admin/ipfs/pins/{cid} (non-panicking CID validator; NO Idempotency-Key)
GET/PUT /admin/system/info (config summary secrets redacted, wired features, scheduler status)

thin_client.shell: One index.html + one ES module + shared api.js, go:embed, served with strict CSP (default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; no external origins), no inline <script>.
thin_client.api_js: reads __Host-csrf cookie, sends X-CSRF-Token on unsafe methods; normalizes problem+json into ApiError; tracks ETag; handles 401/403/429; generates Idempotency-Key for invite + backup run/restore.
thin_client.panel: Client-side step machine driven by GET /api/v1/me/onboarding. Deletes /panel/passkey flag toggle (set server-side on successful registration). New surfaces: keys, proofs+verify, credentials, sessions, tokens (incl create via POST /me/tokens), profile links reorder, publish toggle, avatar, export, deletion request.
thin_client.admin: Session-cookie auth like panel [supersedes bearer-only AdminGuard HTML-form gap]. Views: dashboard, tenants, users+invite, clients+secret rotation, backups, moderation, audit, IPFS pins, system info, deletion requests.

phases.0: Prerequisites: P-1 scope matching (alone, wave 1), P-2 sessions (config-gated dual-read), P-3 CSRF (incl form-encoded no-JS), P-4 migrations (incl pending_deletions), P-5 store methods, config options (dual_read + cors_origins). Exit: migration up/down tests, scope table test incl profile:read-only regression, concurrent session-revoke race test, dual-read overlap test, CSRF form-encoded matrix.
phases.1: Foundation: api/problem, api/dto, route table (scope + timeout per route), full middleware chain, OpenAPI skeleton + drift test, /meta/*, /health, /ready, auth & session endpoints, server assembly (mount /api/v1). Exit: drift test fails on deliberately-omitted route, middleware order test, no-route-without-scope test, server assembly smoke test.
phases.2: Self API: identity/profile/keys/proofs/sessions handlers (direct on store) + all /me/* (incl POST /me/tokens, DELETE /me -> pending_deletions). Wires internal/keys and internal/proofs. Exit: scope matrix, ETag-on-GET tests, cross-tenant IDOR matrix returns 404, token create show-once.
phases.3: Admin API: tenants/clients/backup/moderation/capabilities handlers (direct on store) + all /admin/* (incl deletion-requests). Backup config genuinely persists + drives Scheduler; long-running restores. Exit: non-admin 403 on every admin route, idempotency replay test (one email), backup config->scheduler-start integration test, deletion-request approve/reject.
phases.4: Public API + truth: /api/v1/public/*, capabilities derived from actual wiring, NodeInfo + README status sourced from it. Exit: every README claim maps to capabilities entry AND passing E2E test.
phases.5: Panel client: web/shared, web/panel, vendored CSS, CSP, embed + asset handler. Exit: asset/CSP header tests, legacyforms no-JS ToS + profile path test (incl CSRF form-encoded).
phases.6: Admin client: web/admin, all admin views (incl deletion requests). Exit: asset/CSP tests, smoke test every admin API route reachable from a view.
phases.7: Decommission: feature-parity gate (every function in panel.go + admin/{users,backup}.go maps to API endpoint + client surface) THEN delete internal/server/panel.go templates, internal/admin/{users,backup}.go HTTP layers; /panel/* and /admin/* become client shells + legacyforms. Exit: deadcode clean, no html/template outside web/ and hyperlink.
phases.8: Hardening & docs: rate limits tuned (per-IP), docs/reference/api/, docs/howto/{user,admin,developer}, ADRs D-1..D-9 (D-4 revised), CHANGELOG (incl dual_read flip-to-false). Exit: load test on /auth/*, docs build, per-package coverage >=80%.

testing_strategy: store-backed handlers: table-driven unit tests vs temp SQLite store, no HTTP, coverage >=90%.
api/dto: golden-file JSON tests (locks wire format).
routing/middleware: httptest matrices — scope x route, CSRF x method x principal x content-type (incl form-encoded no-JS), tenant A vs B for every tenant-scoped resource.
contract: bidirectional OpenAPI drift test (kin-openapi test-only dep); response-validation test per handler.
idempotency/concurrency: replay tests (one email, same token); -race on invite redeem, session revoke, link reorder, first-admin.
negative_security: missing/expired/wrong-audience/wrong-issuer tokens; bearer+cookie together -> 400; oversized -> 413; cross-origin unsafe -> 403; dual-read both-formats -> 400.
thin_clients: asset/CSP header assertions in Go. No browser E2E [USER-APPROVED decision 7].
capabilities_truth: capabilities subset features with passing E2E tests, README claims subset capabilities.
deletion_flow: request -> pending -> admin approve -> cascade; reject -> no-op.
timeout: slow backup restore not killed by default per-route timeout.
observability: Structured slog access log: request ID, principal ID (never token), tenant, route pattern, status, duration, bytes.
Audit-log writes for every state-changing admin action AND security-relevant self action (ToS accept, credential add/remove, session revoke, key revoke, token issue), with real actor from P-2.
/api/v1/admin/system/info surfaces scheduler status, last backup error, migration version, wired capabilities.
risks: Scope/permission regression during ScopesContains rewrite -> land P-1 alone with regression test per call site.
Session rework locks users out -> P-2 dual-read gated by auth.session.dual_read (default TRUE), then operator flips to false and drops old JWT cookies.
CSRF breaks scripted clients or no-JS forms -> bearer path exempt by design (D-6); hidden csrf_token field for form-encoded no-JS POSTs; document in CHANGELOG.
Endpoint sprawl -> no-route-without-scope + OpenAPI drift tests make untested routes structurally hard to merge.
Thin client becomes a de-facto framework -> hard cap: no build step, no npm, one shared module.
Coverage dilution -> thin handlers, coverage concentrates in store/.
Long-running backup restore killed by default timeout -> per-route timeout column; backup run/restore long-running.
